title: Grateful Dead Live at Harding Theater on 1971-11-07

ai_review.summary: A stellar 1971 performance with smoking Dark Star, NFA>GDTRFB>NFA and a beautiful Comes‑a‑Time; the soundboard capture is good but shows occasional piano distortion and dropouts.
ai_review.review: This show captures one of the band’s high‑water marks in late ’71 – the second set rolls from a blazing Dark Star into an unforgettable Not Fade Away > Going Down the Road > Not Fade Away sequence, with a gorgeous Comes‑a‑Time and tight jams throughout.  The pre‑FM soundboard source is generally clear and well‑balanced, though listeners note early‑set dropouts and a bit of piano distortion that eases later in the set.  Overall the musical energy and standout moments far outweigh the minor technical quirks.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the performance 4‑5 stars, praising the music and energy; recording issues are mentioned but not enough to outweigh the show quality, yielding a strong combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Pre‑FM board with occasional tape dropouts (e.g., Brown Eyed Woman) and early‑set piano distortion; later tracks clear, low hiss, overall listenable.

standout_songs: Not Fade Away > Going Down the Road > Not Fade Away
show_quality.setlist_flow: Second‑set transitions are praised, especially the NFA>GDTRFB>NFA sequence; first set drives well with strong openings and tight jams.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly described as “on fire,” delivering shining versions of Sugaree, Cumberland Blues, Loser and Comes a Time; dominates the mix in a positive way.
band_member_comments.Phil: Highlighted for being high in the mix, driving the groove on Dark Star and other jams; praised for powerful bass work.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s piano noted as honky‑tonk; early distortion issues mentioned but later sounds clear and adds character to the performance.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann praised for hard‑driving grooves, especially on Dark Star and The Other One.
